div.head: II Ew 5.2
div.ab: Gyf hine hwa feormige syððan, bete swa seo domboc secge, ⁊ se scyle ðe flyman feormie, gyf hit sy herinne; gif hit sy east inne, gif hit sy norð inne, bete be ðam ðe ða friðgewritu secgan.
Gif hine hwa feormige syððan, bete swa seo domboc sæcge, ⁊ se scyle ðe flyman feormige, gif hit sy herinne; gif hit sy east inne, gif hit sy norð inne, bete be ðam þe þa friðgehwritu sæcgan.

Si quis eum deinceps firmabit, emendet sicut liber iudiciorum docet, ac debet qui flyman (id est forisbannitum) confirmabit, si sit hic intus; si sit east intro, si sit nord intus, emendet sicut scripta pacis continent.
Gif hine hwa feormige syððan, bete swa seo domboc sæcge, ⁊ se scyle ðe flyman feormige, gif hit sy herinne; gif hit sy east inne, gif hit sy norð inne, bete be ðam þe þa friðgewritu sæcgen.

If anyone subsequently harbours him, he shall pay such compensation as the written laws declare of him who harbours a fugitive, if the offence is committed in his own kingdom. If the offence is committed in the eastern or northern kingdoms, compensation shall be paid in accordance with the provision of the treaties.

Wenn ihn einer nachher beherbergt, büsse er so, wie das Gesetzbuch besagt, und [zwar, wie] der, welcher einen Geächteten beherbergt, [büssen] muss, falls es hier im [Englischen] Innenlande geschieht; wenn es im Ost[anglischen Lande] geschieht, [oder] wenn es im Nord[humbrischen Lande] geschieht, büsse er gemäss dem, was die Friedensartikel [mit den Nordleuten vereinbart] besagen.

If anyone afterwards harbours him, let him pay compensation as the law-book says, and [namely as] he who harbours an outlaw must [pay], if it happens here in the [English] inland; if it happens in the East[-Anglian land], [or] if it happens in the North[umbrian land], let him pay according to what the peace-articles [agreed with the Northmen] say.

note.label: refers to
note.quote: The second of these provisions can be taken to refer to Ine's law on 'fliemanfeorm (fugitive harbouring)'

note.label: closer in wording to
note.quote: the wording of Edward's supposed citation of Ine's law ('de flieman feormige') was actually closer to that of the rubric than to that of Ine's text
